articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is warping the video game release calendar
articles.summary: The months ahead of GTA’s November launch are becoming increasingly crowded.
articles.body: Who’s afraid of the next GTA? Based on the last few days of Summer Game Fest, just about everyone. Grand Theft Auto VI hasn’t been present at any of the keynote events, but its presence was felt every time a release date was announced. The month of November, when GTA VI launches, is virtually empty. The rest of the fall, meanwhile, is absolutely packed. It started at Sony’s State of Play showcase on Tuesday. Even before that show, we knew that Wolverine, the next big PlayStation exclusive, would be launching on September 15th. But now it’s joined by a bunch of major third-party titles: Dune: Awakening (September 22nd), Control Resonant (September 24th), Silent Hill: Townfall (September 24th), Onimusha: Way of the Sword (September 25th), and Ace Combat 8 (October 2nd). This is on top of other games launching before November that had already been announced, like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in October. Meanwhile, at SGF Live this evening, many of the biggest games went even further out, with planned launches in 2027. That includes: Sega’s crime epic Stranger Than Heaven and its Virtua Fighter spinoff Crossroads; Bandai Namco’s Gundam Rogue Orbit; Capcom’s “massive expansion” for Monster Hunter Wilds; Clutch, the debut Forza-like racer from Maverick Games; and Telltale’s The Wolf Among Us 2. The big reveal of the evening, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, won’t be out until next spring. And while Xbox’s keynote doesn’t take place until Sunday, it has already moved things out of GTA’s way. When it announced that Fable would be delayed yet again, this time until 2027, Microsoft said that part of the reasoning is that this “year is packed with incredible games,” and then cited GTA VI by name, in addition to other titles. [Media: Of course, not all of these titles changed their date specifically because of GTA, but at least some of them did. This also isn’t an entirely new phenomenon. Last year, when Silksong got its surprise September release date, other indie titles shifted their plans to stay clear of it. In some ways, GTA VI is similar, as it’s a long-in-development follow-up to a massive hit. But GTA is also obviously on a much larger scale: These aren’t small indie studios changing their plans, they’re some of the biggest publishers in the industry, including Sony, Microsoft, and Capcom. The reasoning makes some amount of sense. GTA VI is as close as there is to a guaranteed hit. It’s the follow-up to a game that has not only sold nearly 230 million copies across three console generations, but also continues to rake in money through a lucrative online mode. It’s entirely likely GTA VI won’t match those lofty numbers, but it’ll still assuredly sell a lot of copies. Strauss Zelnick, CEO of GTA publisher Take-Two, said in a recent earnings call that he expects to “establish new record levels of operating performance driven by the November 19th launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.” Even the suggestion of a new GTA VI trailer is enough to get the internet frothing. But when everyone has the same idea to avoid November, it creates a different kind of problem: There’s a complete logjam of major releases over the next few months, particularly in September, when several major games are now coming out on the exact same day. Is that really any better than being in the vicinity of GTA? [Media: When The Verge asked Control Resonant creative director Mikael Kasurinen about this at a recent preview event, he seemed undeterred by the sheer number of games launching in the same window. “We’re confident in our game,” he explained. “We feel like we’re in a good place, we have a very distinctive, unique experience, and we believe in that.” Of course, there’s one notable absence from that list of companies dodging GTA, and that’s Nintendo. The company hasn’t yet detailed its holiday plans, and has instead focused on upcoming titles launching soon, like Star Fox (June 25th), Rhythm Heaven Groove (July 2nd) and Splatoon Raiders (July 23rd). But beyond that the calendar is empty, so there’s almost certainly a big announcement (or announcements) coming up that will reveal the games that will power the Switch 2 through the all-important holiday season. If there’s one company that would buck industry trends and launch a major title in November, it would be Nintendo. Additional reporting by Kallie Plagge.

articles.title: GTA VI is getting an ‘extended look’ at the end of August
articles.summary: Rockstar is airing an “extended look” at Grand Theft Auto 6, which will air on both YouTube and Netflix.
articles.body: We’ll be getting an in-depth preview of Grand Theft Auto VI very soon: Rockstar announced this morning that it will be airing an “extended look” at the game on August 27th. The preview will stream on YouTube at 9PM ET, as per usual, but will also be shown earlier for Netflix subscribers, premiering at 3PM ET. (Netflix and Rockstar previously partnered to release the original GTA trilogy on mobile.) There are no other details just yet. “The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first,” Brandon Riegg, Netflix’s VP of Nonfiction Series, said in a statement. Of course, the new GTA has been on the way for quite some time, and is launching well over a decade after GTA V, which went on to become one of the best-selling games of all time, launching across three console generations and PC. As of May, GTA V has sold “nearly” 230 million copies, according to Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two, and it remains a force on Steam and Twitch to this day. Rockstar confirmed it was working on a successor in 2022, and following a massive leak of gameplay videos, the studio released the first GTA VI trailer in 2023. That was followed by a second that came out last year. Here are the previous two trailers for reference: [Media: [Media: Rockstar hasn’t been entirely quiet in the years between GTA V and VI, releasing steady updates for GTA Online along with a little game called Red Dead Redemption 2. But the anticipation for the next GTA has still had plenty of time to build up. And after a few delays, GTA VI is finally slated to launch on the PS5 and Xbox on November 19th, a release date that has forced most other developers and publishers to move out of the way.

articles.title: Why Dolly Parton meant so much to Black communities: Black stars remember a one-of-a-kind icon
articles.summary: Through her career, personality and philanthropy, Dolly Parton built a legacy that transcended music, race and genre. This week, communities
articles.body:
Through her career, personality and philanthropy, Dolly Parton built a legacy that transcended music, race and genre.

This week, communities are grieving the death of country icon, community champion, and philanthropist Dolly Parton . Throughout her career, the 80-year-old style icon became a beloved figure in pop culture. However, the "Jolene" singer held a special place in the hearts of Black communities for a number of reasons. While many recognized her for bold, often bedazzled, sartorial choices and her country catalog, Parton was known for giving back, especially to underserved communities.

For instance, after Whitney Houston covered her 1974 song "I Will Always Love You," Parton used some of the $10 million she received in royalties to invest in a Black neighborhood in Nashville. Purchasing a commercial complex in the area, the country singer said she considered it "the house that Whitney built." Similarly, she was a supporter of the Black Lives Matter movement following the death of George Floyd, and reportedly spent years donating band uniforms to high schools in Tennessee.

Parton was also among the first public figures to advocate for people living with HIV and AIDS in the 80s, and was invested in inspiring children to love reading through her organization, Imagination Library, a free book-gifting program that mails one age-appropriate book each month to children from birth until they turn five years old, including audio and braille books for children who are blind or visually impaired. This work, paired with her charming personality and consistent respect and support for Black artists from Whitney Houston to Three 6 Mafia to Beyoncé, is part of why Black communities love her so deeply. In an often divisive world, Parton managed to operate in a way that made it impossible for anyone to put her in just any box other than her own, making her an inspiration to many.

And these Black celebrities are honoring Parton's legacy.

"Dolly, you were the barometer. The North Star, bold and brilliant. talented and tenacious. You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself. I am grateful for your art, your heart, your generosity, your humor, your entrepreneurship. I'm honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever. Thank you for your profound impact on the world. You are an angel who has made this world a happier place because of your joyful art. You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully."

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of the incomparable Dolly Parton. Dolly was a true trailblazer. Through her extraordinary talent, kindness and generosity, she opened doors and inspired generations around the world. We share this special memory from 1977, when we had the honor of meeting Dolly in England on the same day we also met Queen Elizabeth II. Thank you, Dolly, for the music, the joy and the light you shared with us all. May you rest peacefully in the loving arms of the Lord, reunited with your husband Carl and the many loved ones who made their journey to Heaven before you. Our prayers are with Dolly's family, friends and everyone whose life she touched."

"Ms Dolly did THAT!! From movies, song writing, amusement park, hotels, charity, SINCERITY, unabashed foxiness, humor…. EVERYTHING. The neighbor I never saw but adored. Sent ❤️ every time I passed her house. Ms Dolly is on my inspo wall. Rest well dear lady; Did GREATNESS HER WAY,' she wrote on X.

"It's hard to imagine many people having a bigger impact than Dolly Parton. Born in a one-room cabin, she earned 11 Grammys and an Emmy, built a business empire, helped millions of kids learn to read, and — as if that wasn't enough — helped accelerate the research that led to the Moderna COVID vaccine. What a life. Michelle and I are thinking of Dolly's family and her many, many fans," former president Barack Obama wrote.

"I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend. My heart is heavy," Dionne Warwick shared.

"She has been my blueprint for how to use your fame and wealth for good. I, of course, am not on her level — or even close — in either measure but I try to model Dolly's goodness and activism in all that I do and in every issue and charity that I support," Brown wrote. "She did life right. I am inconsolable over this loss."

"The bastion of compassion, of altruism, authenticity, artistry, and love has left this life. You knew who you were… always… without apology, without a co-signer, without needing permission. And oh, how you were blessed with talent," Viola Davis wrote on Instagram. "No words to describe your reach through generations. No words to describe your love force. No words to describe the lives you touched, saved, entertained, and shifted. God will be at the gates to welcome you with the most glorious tribute. Your family, colleagues, friends, fellow artists… will keep you alive and speak your name… forever. Rest well, Dolly Parton. WHAT A LIFE!!!!!"

"Dolly taught us that you can be anything and do anything and to do it with kindness. What a light. We are all grateful that we lived in a time of Dolly Parton. We will always love her."

"One of my fondest memories with @dollyparton: Having a hoot and a holler while wearing Bob Mackie gowns on her show Dolly," the media mogul wrote on Instagram. "This girl from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee dreamed a life and then lived a life bigger than she could have ever imagined, giving so generously to others in ways we saw and ways we didn't. No one like her. She brought the light, and we are all better because she was here. God bless you, Dolly—you earned your wings

"Dolly Parton was a true American icon. First introduced to the world as a "little girl from up in East Tennessee," she became a global superstar. Her career accolades included 11 Grammy awards, an Emmy, an honorary Oscar, and — my favorite — more than 300 million books sent to millions of children around the world through her Imagination Library," Harris wrote on Instagram. "All at once, she was kind, modest, and funny. With her music, her philanthropy, and her style, Dolly was one of one. Doug and I send our prayers to her family, friends, and all those who have been touched by her magic. We will always love you, Dolly."

"There are some people who remind you just how powerful it is to be completely and unapologetically yourself. Dolly Parton was one of those people. She showed generations of women that you could be bold, feminine, ambitious, kind, funny, and entirely your own person. She never seemed interested in fitting into anyone else's idea of who she should be, and I've always found that incredibly empowering," Tia Mowry wrote on Instagram. "What a beautiful reminder to embrace what makes you different, take up space, and move through this world as your most authentic self. Thank you, Dolly, for showing us the power of individuality and for inspiring so many of us to own exactly who we are. Rest in peace, Dolly. Your light will live on"

"Dolly you were a gift to the world, your voice, your philanthropic heart, and warmth made us a feel seen and that the world was a pretty decent place. We miss you."

articles.title: FAC DF: Governo suspende edital por falta de verba | G1
articles.standfirst: Em publicação do Diário Oficial, Secretaria de Cultura alega falta de recursos para contratação de banca examinadora. Valor estimado é de R$ 992,7 mil.
articles.summary: A Secretaria de Cultura suspendeu a seleção do FAC DF alegando falta de recursos, enquanto o TCDF investiga o bloqueio de R$ 79,5 milhões destinados ao setor.
articles.body:
A Secretaria de Cultura do Distrito Federal suspendeu nesta quinta-feira (27) o edital do Fundo de Apoio à Cultura (FAC) lançado no início do ano. O motivo: falta de verba.

A decisão foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Distrito Federal desta quinta e não dá qualquer prazo para a retomada das contratações.

Segundo a secretaria, não há disponibilidade de orçamento para contratar a banca responsável pela análise de mérito cultural dos projetos inscritos . O valor da contratação é de R$ 992,7 mil.

O cancelamento se soma a uma série de problemas no financiamento de projetos culturais no DF desde o início do ano.

Na segunda-feira (25), o Tribunal de Contas do Distrito Federal (TCDF) determinou o prazo de cinco dias para que a Secretaria e a Secec prestem esclarecimentos sobre o contingenciamento de e R$ 79,5 milhões destinados ao FAC .

O valor corresponde a 86% dos R$ 91,9 milhões previstos para o programa por meio da Lei Orçamentária Anual de 2026.

📖 A medida, no entanto, fere a Lei Orgânica da Cultura, que veda o contingenciamento ou remanejamento dos recursos do FAC.

Questionada, a Secretaria de Cultura afirma que a gestão dos repasses é de responsabilidade da Economia.

"A Secec tem adotado todas as medidas administrativas sob sua responsabilidade e mantém interlocução permanente com a Secretaria de Economia para viabilizar a liberação dos recursos e garantir a continuidade da execução dos projetos do FAC, em observância à legislação vigente", declara.

Autor da representação contra o contingenciamento no Tribunal de Contas, o deputado distrital Gabriel Magno (PT) afirma que já adicionou o cancelamento do edital ao processo.

"É mais uma evidência e uma prova da nossa tese de que eles estão bloqueando ilegalmente o dinheiro do FAC", afirma.

Leia a íntegra da nota divulgada pela Secretaria de Cultura sobre a suspensão do FAC:

A Secretaria de Cultura e Economia Criativa do Distrito Federal informa que o Edital nº 06/2026 – FAC I/2026 – Demais Áreas foi temporariamente suspenso em razão da indisponibilidade orçamentária para a contratação dos pareceristas responsáveis pela análise de mérito cultural dos projetos inscritos.

A suspensão é temporária. O certame será retomado assim que houver desbloqueio e/ou disponibilização de recursos orçamentários e financeiros suficientes para garantir a continuidade da seleção.

A Secec-DF reforça que a retomada do edital e eventual novo cronograma serão divulgados oficialmente no Diário Oficial do Distrito Federal e no site da Subsecretaria de Fomento e Incentivo Cultural (Sufic).

O bloqueio orçamentário impacta não só o FAC de 2026, que estava em fase de análise, mas também os editais de 2025.

Cineastas contemplados no FAC Audiovisual do ano passado alegam ainda não terem recebido a verba prevista para a execução dos projetos.

O Distrito Federal foi contemplado pelo Edital Arranjos Regionais, do Ministério da Cultura, mas corre risco de não conseguir os recursos previstos.

Isso porque a Secretaria de Cultura precisa pagar uma contrapartida de R$ 6 milhões ao Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual (FSA). Apenas após o pagamento, o DF pode receber os recursos do edital, equivalente a R$ 30 milhões.

Cine Brasília — Foto: Agência Brasília/Reprodução

A falta de repasses chegou a ameaçar o 59ª Festival de Brasília do Cinema Brasileiro. O governo chegou a informar em uma reunião fechada que tinha cancelado edição por falta de verbas, mas voltou atrás após repercussão negativa .

Em julho, a falta de repasse atingiu o próprio Cine Brasília, último cinema de rua do Distrito Federal e maior do país.

O espaço é a sede do Festival de Cinema de Brasília desde a criação e, sem recursos, correu o risco de fechar as portas.

À época, os gestores afirmam que a situação já afetava o pagamento de funcionários e fornecedores – e poderia comprometer o próprio funcionamento do cinema.

O cancelamento por falta de dinheiro seria algo sem precedentes nas seis décadas de festival.

🎥 Criado em 1965, o Festival de Brasília é o mais antigo festival de cinema do Brasil.

🎥 O evento só não foi realizado entre 1972 e 1974, em protesto contra a ditadura militar. As edições foram mantidas mesmo durante a pandemia de Covid-19, em formato virtual.

🎥Desde 2007, o festival é considerado "patrimônio imaterial do Distrito Federal".

articles.title: Rolê no Alto Tietê: fim de semana tem shows de Mc Lele JP, Silvero Pereira e stand-up com Vini Maga | G1
articles.standfirst: Shows, stand-up, teatro e cinema estão entre as opções para aproveitar os próximos dias no Alto Tietê.
articles.summary: Shows, stand-up, teatro e cinema estão entre as opções para aproveitar os próximos dias no Alto Tietê.
articles.body:
A agenda cultural do Alto Tietê tem shows, peças de teatro, apresentações de humor e sessões de cinema nos próximos dias. Entre os destaques estão MC Lele JP, Silvero Pereira e Vini Maga, além da programação do 2º Festival de Cinema Itapety, em Mogi das Cruzes .

Na música, a programação tem shows de Karen Santana e DJ VZK, Rolls Rock, Crossbar Rock, Val Pinheiro e Sollano. As apresentações incluem diferentes gêneros e repertórios.

Os fãs de cinema também podem aproveitar a última semana do 2º Festival de Cinema Itapety, que reúne produções regionais e nacionais em diferentes espaços de Mogi das Cruzes.

Na comédia, a programação tem shows de stand-up com Confraria Comedy, Guto Andrade e Menino do RH.

No teatro, a programação tem os espetáculos "O Mundo de Papel", da Trupe BorboLetras; "Victor e Brutus", da The Pambazos Bros; "Véi Mané (ou de quando abrir os olhos)", da Cia do Escândalo; e "Dinossauros do Brasil", da Pia Fraus.

A programação também tem exposições e outros eventos. Há opções gratuitas e pagas.

articles.title: Quem é Tini Stoessel, cantora argentina que rompeu com o pai | G1
articles.standfirst: Revelada pela série “Violetta”, da Disney, artista argentina construiu carreira na música, lançou cinco álbuns e tem parceria com Anitta.
articles.summary: Revelada pela série “Violetta”, da Disney, artista argentina construiu carreira na música, lançou cinco álbuns e tem parceria com Anitta.
articles.body:
Tini Stoessel — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Martina “Tini” Stoessel, que encerrou sua relação profissional com seu pai após 15 anos, é uma cantora e atriz argentina de sucesso na América Latina.

Ela começou a carreira com 14 anos como protagonista da série "Violetta", do canal Disney Channel. O sucesso infanto-juvenil resultou em shows espalhados pela Améica Latina, inclusive no Brasil.

Em 2016, já no processo de deixar a personagem para trás, ela protagonizou o filme “Tini: Depois de Violetta”, também produção da Disney.

Um ano após o fim do programa, ela deu início à carreira musical e hoje acumula cinco álbuns lançados. Em 2022, Tini, Anitta e Becky G lançaram "La Loto". Ela também tem parcerias com Christina Aguilera e Flo Rida.

A cantora tem mais de 22 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais.

No âmbito pessoal, Tini é noiva do jogador Rodrigo de Paul, também argentino, que atua no Inter Miami.

Tini Stoessel e Rodrigo De Paul — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Após a decisão de cortar laços com o pai, a artista pediu para que fosse realizada uma revisão nos contratos, contas e empresas ligadas a seu nome.

De acordo com a publicação do La Nación, a auditoria teria revelado que o pai de Stoessel era o único beneficiário de seus ganhos, com uma soma que chega a US$ 70 milhões (cerca de R$ 361 milhões).

O jornal entrou em contato com Alejandro Stoessel, mas o produtor não respondeu às mensagens.

Nem a cantora nem a mãe, Mariana Muzlera, se pronunciaram publicamente sobre a separação empresarial.

O jornalista Damián Rojo explicou que a cantora assinou documentos confiando em quem os apresentava, sem conhecer o teor do que estava escrito.

A cantora teria um limite de gastos mensais de US$ 5.000 em seu cartão de crédito pessoal. De acordo com fontes do jornal, um argumento para concentrar o dinheiro nas mãos do pai residia na proteção da jovem contra possíveis reivindicações legais externas.

A investigação interna teria começado a pedido do jogador argentino Rodrigo de Paul, noivo de Tini. Segundo o programa "Secretos Verdaderos", o atleta sugeriu a revisão dos detalhes financeiros depois que seu sogro solicitou um acordo pré-nupcial. Diante disso, a cantora percebeu sua falta de controle financeiro.

Por enquanto, não há nenhuma queixa formal por fraude ou administração fraudulenta.

O jornalista Damián Rojo explicou que a cantora assinou documentos confiando em quem os apresentava, sem conhecer o teor do que estava escrito. “Em alguns casos, e a pedido das próprias empresas contratantes, ela afirmou que aceitava o envolvimento dessas empresas. Mas ela nunca cedeu seus direitos a elas, nem seus direitos de imagem, nem seus direitos comerciais.

Ela assinou esses documentos sem conhecer o seu alcance total, confiando em quem os apresentou a ela. As empresas controladas por Alejandro acumulam o dinheiro gerado pelo trabalho da jovem, e ela não consta como autorizada a fazer transações bancárias em nenhuma dessas empresas”, afirmou ele. A artista só teve acesso à sua própria conta em junho de 2026, após a intervenção de advogados.

“La Nacion” explicou ainda que, por enquanto, não há nenhuma queixa formal por fraude ou administração fraudulenta.

articles.title: Vicentina pede desculpas: Gabriel Martins fala de novo filme e Oscar | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista ao g1, cineasta mineiro falou sobre paralelos entre seu 2º filme solo e obra de Kleber Mendonça Filho, cinema nacional e Oscar. 'Vicentina' estreia em 5 de novembro.
articles.summary: Gabriel Martins analisa o luto em Vicentina pede desculpas, novo filme do diretor de Marte Um que chega aos cinemas e à Netflix após pré-seleção para o Oscar.
articles.body:
Rejane Faria em cena de 'Vicentina pede desculpas' — Foto: Denize dos Santos/Netflix

Demorou quatro anos, mas finalmente o celebrado diretor de "Marte Um" (2022), Gabriel Martins, vai lançar seu próximo filme. "Vicentina pede desculpas" , segundo projeto solo do cineasta mineiro de 38 anos, vai estrear nos cinemas brasileiros em 5 de novembro .

A obra, uma das 15 pré-selecionadas pela Academia Brasileira de Cinema para talvez representar o país no Oscar 2027 , antes disso ainda participa de competições em festivais como o de San Sebastián e o de Toronto, em setembro.

Em "Vicentina pede desculpas", Martins se reencontra com parceiros de "Marte Um", como Rejane Faria e Renato Novaes para contar a história de uma mãe que precisa lidar com luto da morte do filho — ao mesmo tempo em que parte em uma jornada para pedir desculpas às famílias dos passageiros do ônibus que ele dirigia.

"É um filme sobre entender assim o luto, a morte dentro de uma estrutura contemporânea de cidade urbana. Nesse caso, Belo Horizonte. E falar também sobre essa coletividade", afirma o diretor ao g1 .

"A gente quer falar dessas conexões humanas. É o desejo desse filme. Para além disso, falar sobre masculinidade, a partir do filho, a partir de encontros que ela tem. E falar sobre maternidade, também, de uma maneira não superficial."

Depois de um período nos cinemas brasileiros, o filme vai ser lançado simultaneamente em mais de 190 países na plataforma de streaming Netflix, em 20 de novembro .

Na entrevista, o cineasta falou sobre os paralelos inesperados com o começo da carreira de outro nome importante do cinema nacional contemporâneo, Kleber Mendonça Filho, as semelhanças de "Vicentina pede desculpas" com "Aquarius" (2016), a expansão do público de obras brasileiras e, claro, o papel do Oscar em tudo isso.

Leia a conversa completa abaixo, editada para clareza:

g1 - Você fez uma sessão de "Marte Um" com mediação do Kleber Mendonça Filho. Pode ser só uma loucura minha, mas eu comecei a ver um certo paralelo entre o seu filme e "O som ao redor", que foi o primeiro dele. Tem uma coisa muito realista, um naturalismo cinematográfico brasileiro nos dois. Ambos foram suas estreias na direção solo, e ambos foram escolhidos para representar o Brasil no Oscar. Dá para falar então que o "Vicentina pede desculpas", sem saber muito sobre o filme, é o seu "Aquarius"?

Gabriel Martins - Nossa, essa pergunta aí foi interessante (risos). Cara, eu não tinha pensado muito sobre essa analogia, né? Embora eu ache que eu me comunico, sim, com o cinema do Kleber de várias formas. Acho que tem uma relação muito forte do cinema do Kleber entre personagem, espaço e a maneira de dialogar cinematograficamente com essas duas coisas, né? Que eu acho muito legal.

Talvez, a coisa que que mais se comunica é o fato de de vir de dois filmes — no caso, "Marte Um" e "O som ao redor" — que são filmes de conjunto, né? De um grupo de personagens. E, dos filmes que eu dirigi, esse é o primeiro filme muito focado em uma personagem. E talvez no caso do "Aquarius" também seja a mesma coisa.

Isso foi uma coisa muito interessante assim para mim. Eu queria mostrar um pouco essa jornada de uma mulher. Focar não só na história dela, mas também visualmente. Para mim era uma coisa muito legal assim pensar que todo dia eu estava acordando e indo para o set para filmar o rosto da Rejane. Mais do que o rosto da Rejane, o rosto dessa personagem. Da Vicentina, né?

Então, acho que com certeza esses filmes se comunicam por um desejo de investigação parecido. E, para mim, esse lugar dessa personagem centralizada.

Fazer um estudo de personagem era uma coisa que eu queria fazer há um tempo. E antes mesmo do "Marte Um", quando eu fiz o "No coração do mundo" (2019), também era um grande conjunto, um filme muito sobre um espaço, sobre uma região que não tem ali uma protagonista ou um protagonista tão bem definido.

Agora não. É uma pessoa mesmo. É a gente passar um tempo com essa pessoa. Enfim, achei sua analogia muito bem-vinda. Eu acho que faz faz sentido, sim.

Primeiro pôster de 'Vicentina pede desculpas' — Foto: Divulgação

g1 - Numa entrevista que eu li, que foi publicada em julho ou junho, se eu não me engano, você ainda fala assim: "Ah, não posso falar muita coisa sobre o filme". A gente já sabe que tem seus parceiros habituais, tem a Rejane, o Renato, a Grace (Passô). É um projeto de mais de 10 anos e eu já vi também você falar que filmou em 2024. O que mais que você pode falar sobre o "Vicentina"?

Gabriel Martins - Acho que é um filme sobre uma personagem, né? Essa personagem Vicentina, que leva o nome da minha avó. E é um filme sobre entender o luto, a morte dentro de uma estrutura contemporânea de cidade urbana. Nesse caso, Belo Horizonte. E falar também sobre essa coletividade. A coletividade como uma uma solução para momentos difíceis como esse.

Acho que isso, principalmente entendendo o nosso mundo. Não vou falar nem só de Brasil ou BH ou grandes cidades, mas o nosso mundo como um mundo que cada dia me parece mais individualizado. As pessoas mais separadas, assim.

Essa jornada individual da Vicentina — ela vai falar também disso. De conexões. O próprio título do filme já traz o gesto do filme, que é uma personagem pedindo desculpa para as pessoas a partir desse acidente. E se entende que o filho dela provocou o acidente como um suicídio.

A gente quer falar dessas conexões humanas. É o desejo desse filme. Para além disso, falar sobre masculinidade, a partir do filho, a partir de encontros que ela tem. E falar sobre maternidade, também, de uma maneira não superficial.

Acho que é um filme que tem o que eu sempre tive o desejo de trazer: a dor mesmo desses encontros.

Se o "Marte Um" era um filme muito, talvez, sobre essa comunicação entre essa família — ou da falha de comunicação —, acho que o Vicentina é de alguma forma também sobre essa possibilidade de escuta, essa possibilidade de perdão em um mundo no qual, na verdade, todo mundo parece estar mais interessado em se atacar, em culpabilizar os outros.

É engraçado, porque é um filme que eu fiquei o tempo todo com medo dele envelhecer. É um projeto tão antigo que para mim eu ficava o tempo todo assim: "Nossa, eu estou tentando fazer esse filme. Estou tentando fazer esse filme. Será que, quando ele existir, ainda vai ser relevante, essas temáticas, esse desejo?"

E acho que me parece que sim. Me parece que talvez não só se manteve relevante como agora, mais que nunca, é um momento muito importante dessa história nascer da maneira que ela é, pelas coisas que ela fala.

g1 - Por que que levou tanto tempo para para para sair?

Gabriel Martins - Eu acho que é um processo natural dentro de uma ideia de cinema independente brasileiro. Que os financiamentos e as oportunidades não são tão óbvias o tempo todo, né? Essa é uma questão.

E eu acho que também esse projeto que ficou escrito, mas dentro de uma produtora como a minha, que tem ali três diretores, vários projetos. Então, eu escrevi esse projeto e nesse meio tempo o "Marte Um" se mostrou como uma possibilidade mais concreta de ser executado primeiro.

Acho que os filmes têm um pouco uma vida própria, um tempo. E acabou fazendo sentido também que eu estivesse um pouco mais maduro para fazer esse projeto no momento que fiz. Com essa parceria com a Netflix que acho que propiciou um volume de produção mais robusto, que deu conta dessa história, que é difícil.

Era um roteiro grande, né? Era um roteiro bem desafiador, muitas locações. Foi um pouco uma mistura de tudo assim: uma mistura desse desafio da gente, principalmente aqui em Minas, não ter tantos editais para longa-metragem sempre. Para projetos robustos como esse, então, nem se fala, né?

Mas eu acho que, no fim das contas, eu também eu respeito muito — e a gente, a produtora, respeita muito — o tempo assim dos processos.

A gente fala assim: "Nossa, demorou muito tempo para fazer", e parece que é sempre num tom de reclamação. Em parte é, né, porque a gente quer que o cinema brasileiro nos dê mais oportunidades.

Mas, ao mesmo tempo, eu acho que também o filme nasce quando ele tem que nascer, da forma como ele tem que nascer. E eu acho que o "Vicentina", é, me parece mais um um exemplo desse, né?

Camilla Damião, Rejane Faria, Cícero Lucas e Carlos Francisco em cena de 'Marte Um' — Foto: Divulgação

g1 - No site da Ancine, diz que "Marte Um" teve um público um pouco menor de 100 mil pessoas.

Gabriel Martins - Foi mais, foi mais de 100 mil pessoas, na verdade.

("A distribuidora me passou o numero de 104.417", afirmou Martins, depois da entrevista. "Tem borderôs que a Ancine não registrou, pois tem salas não cadastradas.")

g1 - Ah, que bom. Porque me parece pouco mesmo. É um dos melhores filmes dos dos dos últimos anos, tranquilamente.

g1 - Como melhorar esse alcance? O filme foi sucesso com a crítica, escolhido para tentar ser o representante do Brasil no Oscar e ainda teve um um público tanto um tanto quanto limitado.

Gabriel Martins - Tentando dar uma resposta complexa um pouco mais compacta aqui (risos), eu acho que a coisa que eu colocaria como simples é o investimento público. Transformar o cinema como parte real e vital da cultura brasileira. Não só o cinema, mas todas as artes.

Entender que o cinema, com essa cadeia produtiva muito ampla e muito cara — a gente não pode deixar que, no fim das contas, fique parecendo que é a culpa do filme ou da distribuidora que não conseguiu fazer o marketing do jeito certo.

Na verdade, é um problema que começa ali nas escolas, né? De criar um interesse e uma cultura. Criar salas de cinema públicas, de repente, que sejam mais acessíveis do que as salas que nós já temos.

Acho que transformar isso de certa forma no patrimônio cultural para que quando, por exemplo, uma Cinemateca Brasileira pegue fogo , isso seja uma questão muito grave, e não seja só mais uma questão que as pessoas nem sabem o que é.

Então, eu acho que existe uma cadeia que precisa agir de várias formas. Existe a disposição disso no mercado brasileiro cinematográfico — pessoas que trabalham com cineclubes, professores, pesquisadores —, e eu acho que existe cada vez mais o interesse das pessoas também em resgatar o cinema brasileiro e assistir o que é feito aqui.

Só que acho que sem investimento — investimento para se poder ter mais salas de cinema, para de fato proteger as salas de cinema e o espaço de cotas para a produção brasileira —, a gente não vai conseguir mudar esse cenário. Então não existe muito uma outra solução, a meu ver, a não ser um investimento muito forte em todas essas cadeias para construir atenção e valorização para o cinema brasileiro.

Rejane Farias e Renato Novaes em cena de 'Vicentina pede desculpas' — Foto: Denize dos Santos/Netflix

g1 - Essa semana saíram lá os os 15 filmes que podem chegar a representar o Brasil no Oscar. "Vicentina" está entre eles. É, aliás, um grande momento do do cinema mineiro. O "Nosso Segredo", do qual você é um dos montadores, também está lá.

g1 - Eu já vi você falando que "toda essa questão de Oscar é legal, mas também não pode ser apenas isso que exista". Mas eu eu sinto também que ela ajuda a trazer a atenção de volta. O público no geral tem essa questão, de olhar o mundo reconhecendo, e aí começa a reconhecer também. O quanto isso pode ajudar também a fomentar esse interesse e a formar o público pelo pelo cinema nacional?

Gabriel Martins - Existe uma visibilidade que é inevitável, né? E jornalisticamente falando, em termos de opinião pública, acho que isso lembra as pessoas que: "Olha, gente, tem o cinema brasileiro forte". Inclusive em outras regiões do país. No Recife, a gente viu aí com "O Agente Secreto". "Marte Um" aconteceu isso, né? De repente começou a se falar mais ainda de cinema mineiro.

Então eu acho que qualquer tipo de destaque, até pensando nos festivais internacionais. O "Nosso Segredo" estava em Berlim, a gente está aí em Toronto, San Sebastián. Eu acho que aos poucos passos a gente vai trazendo atenção, mas a única coisa que eu sinto é que não pode ser só isso.

Porque, se for só isso, vai continuar sendo exceção e êxitos individuais dos filmes e de produções que têm modelos muito específicos. Eu acho que o que a gente tem que tentar, nesse volume de atenção que o Brasil tem tido em premiações nos últimos dois anos, realmente fomentar tudo isso que eu já falei na resposta anterior, né? De algo que de fato sedimente espaço até para novos talentos.

Novas produtoras que estão surgindo por aí, tanta gente legal que não necessariamente vai nesse momento já da sua carreira chegar lá no Oscar com o primeiro filme, mas eu acho que merece também ter seu espaço, merece também ter um público maior do que o do "Marte Um".

Eu acho que a gente precisa realmente construir esse caminho simplesmente porque eu acho que a gente merece, assim. A cultura brasileira e o cinema brasileiro merecem por tudo que vêm fazendo.

articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer 'Ramayana’ earns praise as 15-minute exclusive footage showcases one-eyed daitya, creatures,  'Hollywood-level VFX at par with The Lord of the Rings'- Report
articles.summary: The much-awaited 'Ramayana' received another boost in anticipation after 15 minutes of previously unreleased footage from the period epic was screened.
articles.body: The much-awaited 'Ramayana' received another boost in anticipation after 15 minutes of previously unreleased footage from the period epic was screened exclusively for exhibitors at Big Cine Expo 2026 in Chennai. Held on August 18 and 19, the exhibition event brought together theatre owners and other cinema industry stakeholders, with the Ramayana presentation taking place on the opening day. According to a Bollywood Hungama report, an exhibitor who attended the screening, the presentation featured footage that has not yet been made available to the public. Mobile phones were reportedly prohibited during the showcase, with attendees instructed not to record any portion of the presentation.'Ramayana’s exclusive 15-minute footage showcased unreleased visualsAn exhibitor who attended the preview shared details of the presentation, describing it as tightly guarded content. "It lasted for 15 minutes and, as expected, visuals from the film that have not yet been revealed to the public were presented to us. Hence, we were strictly prohibited from using our mobile phones or recording any part of the presentation," the exhibitor said.Detailing what the footage showed, the report revealed that several of the film's creature designs took centre stage. "The major highlights were the various creatures in the film, including the one-eyed daitya. A bear-like creature was also given prominence. We were amazed by the vision, imagination and VFX. Ramayana truly looks like a global Indian film. Its effects are at par with those of any Hollywood movie, like The Lord Of The Rings. The trailer had already excited the exhibitors, and this footage preview has added to the hype for us," the exhibitor added.According to the exhibitor, the preview wasn't limited to raw footage alone. "The asset was also like a making-of video. In between, quotes from producer Namit Malhotra were incorporated, in which he spoke about his ambitious endeavour. Finally, the Ramayana trailer, which has been out since July 30, formed the last part of the 15-minute preview," the exhibitor said, as quoted by the publication, indicating that the presentation combined new visuals with existing promotional material to give attendees a fuller picture of the project's scale.'Ramayana' trailer formed the final part of the presentationThe 'Ramayana' trailer, released on July 30, was shown towards the conclusion of the 15-minute presentation. The exhibitor said the trailer formed the final portion of the showcase, effectively bringing together the newly presented material and the footage already available to the public. The screening therefore offered exhibitors an extended look at the film's visual treatment while keeping the unreleased material away from public circulation.Ranbir Kapoor and Yash headline 'Ramayana: The Introduction'Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, 'Ramayana' stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, with Rakul Preet Singh, Lara Dutta, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil and Indira Krishnan rounding out the ensemble cast. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is being backed by Prime Focus's VFX studio DNEG, with music composed jointly by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.The film's first trailer, released on July 30, was unveiled at San Diego Comic-Con, where Tiwari, Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Malhotra were present to discuss the making of the project. During the event, Tiwari confirmed that Ramayana: Part 1 will end on a cliffhanger, setting up the abduction of Sita as the story's pivot point heading into Part 2. Ranbir Kapoor has also revealed that the two-part saga will together run to nearly six hours of screen time. articles.title: Top Gear to return after Andrew Flintoff's crash, BBC confirms
articles.summary: The show was "rested" after co-host Andrew Flintoff was injured in a crash during filming in 2022.
articles.body:
Top Gear is to return to TV, the BBC has confirmed, four years after the show was "rested" when co-host Andrew Flintoff was injured in a crash during filming.

The long-running motoring programme has been off air since 2022, when the former cricketer suffered serious facial and rib injuries when his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned at the show's test track.

He was one of three presenters at the time along with Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris.

The hosting line-up for the comeback has not yet been announced, although the Sun newspaper last week reported that comedian Jimmy Carr was in talks to join.

The BBC's director of entertainment Ed Havard told the Edinburgh TV Festival on Thursday: "There has been a lot of speculation about this and we can confirm that Top Gear is coming back.

"I'm not going to talk about talent today."

Asked whether Jimmy Carr would be hosting, he replied: "Jimmy would be a great host but I won't be discussing that today.

"We will have more information on Top Gear shortly."

Former rugby player and Celebrity Traitors star Joe Marler is also reportedly in the frame to host.

The show will be made by BBC Studios, which did not comment further.

Top Gear began in 1977 and became one of the BBC's biggest hits in the hands of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May in the 2000s.

They were replaced by broadcaster Chris Evans and Friends star Matt LeBlanc, before Flintoff, McGuinness and Harris took over in 2018.

The BBC apologised and paid compensation to Flintoff following his crash.

He has described being dragged face-down underneath the Morgan Super 3 car for about 50 metres. "I thought I was dead," he told a Disney+ documentary last year .

Paul Rees, a racing driver and expert adviser who was in the car with Flintoff, has sued BBC Studios for up to £150,000 for personal injury. BBC Studios has said: "We dispute this claim and are defending it."

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s six-decade love story with Carl Dean began at a laundromat
articles.summary: Dolly Parton and Carl Dean's private love story began at a Nashville laundromat in 1964 and endured nearly 60 years away from the spotlight.
articles.body: Dolly Parton lived much of her life in the spotlight, but her greatest love story unfolded almost entirely away from it. The country music legend, who died on Tuesday at the age of 80 after a "brief battle with cancer," was married for almost 60 years to her late husband Carl Dean. Parton's death comes less than 18 months after she lost Dean, who died in March 2025 at age 82. While announcing her passing, her nephew Bryan Seaver shared their family's belief that she had been reunited with the man she called the "star of my life story." TRUMP MOURNS DOLLY PARTON, ORDERS US FLAGS LOWERED NATIONWIDE AFTER COUNTRY MUSIC ICON DIES "Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed to meet her in the heavens," Seaver said. Despite being married to the internationally famous singer, Dean was a very private man who steered clear of the limelight and was rarely seen in public. The couple's romance began with a chance meeting on Parton's first day in Nashville in 1964. At the time, Parton was 18 and Dean was 21. Parton, who hailed from rural East Tennessee, previously shared she had been so eager to leave home that she arrived in Nashville with dirty clothes and went to the Wishy Washy Laundromat. While her clothes were in the wash, she bought a cold drink and walked around looking at her new city. Dean drove past in a Chevrolet and warned her that she was going to get sunburned. Parton, who said she greeted everyone because she was "straight from the country," answered him. He soon circled back and joined her at the laundromat. "I was surprised and delighted that while he talked to me, he looked at my face, a rare thing for me," Parton recalled in a 2016 post on her official website. "He seemed to be genuinely interested in finding out who I was and what I was about." During his lifetime, Dean rarely gave interviews. However, in 2016, he spoke lovingly of Parton while the couple were celebrating their 50th wedding anniversary. "My first thought was, 'I'm going to marry that girl,'" Dean told Entertainment Tonight about meeting Parton for the first time. "My second thought was, 'Lord, she’s good-looking.' And that was the day my life began. I wouldn't trade the last 50 years for nothing on this Earth." Two years after their first meeting, Parton and Dean married in a private ceremony in Ringgold, Georgia, on May 30, 1966. Parton’s record label had reportedly urged her to postpone the wedding for a year while launching her career, but the couple chose to marry quietly across the state line to avoid coverage in the Nashville press. Parton's mother, Avie Lee, was the only wedding guest. "It was just my mother and Carl and me," Parton told CMT in 2016. "We went across the state line to Ringgold, Georgia. My mother made me a little white dress and a little bouquet and a little Bible." Parton said she rejected the idea of a courthouse ceremony because she feared she would not "feel married." The couple instead found a small Baptist church, where Pastor Don Duvall married them before they posed for photographs on its steps. According to Parton’s official website, the pastor’s wife also attended. While Parton pursued her dream of country music stardom, Dean remained firmly outside the entertainment industry. He owned an asphalt-paving business in Nashville and preferred a quiet life on their farm away from the limelight, though Parton said he always supported her ambitions. Early in their marriage, Parton persuaded Dean to accompany her to the BMI Awards, where she won her first songwriting award for 1966's "Put It Off Until Tomorrow," which was named song of the year. During a December 2024 appearance on Bunnie Xo’s "Dumb Blonde" podcast, Parton recalled renting Dean a tuxedo and begging him to attend. "And, oh, he was so uncomfortable the whole night," Parton said. DOLLY PARTON’S ONGOING HEALTH BATTLE FORCES COUNTRY LEGEND TO MISS MAJOR DOLLYWOOD EVENT Parton remembered that Dean "started pulling off stuff" immediately after they returned home. "He said, ‘Look, now I want you to do everything you want to do, and I wish you the best, but don't ever ask me to go to another one of these damn things because I ain't going.’ And he never did," she said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER "So we just kind of have that respect, and I respected that because I didn't know he was gonna be that uneasy, but he doesn't even like to go out to, you know, to big dinners or anything like that," she added. Over time, Dean's absence became so conspicuous that there was speculation that he didn't exist, and she had made him up to ward off admirers. During a 2020 interview with Entertainment Tonight, Parton weighed in on the longtime rumors. "A lot of people have thought that through the years, because he does not want to be in the spotlight at all," she shared. "It's just not who he is. He's like, a quiet, reserved person and he figured if he ever got out there in that, he'd never get a minute’s peace and he's right about that." "I've always respected and appreciated that in him and I've always tried to keep him out of the limelight as much as I can," Parton continued. "He said, 'I didn't choose this world, I chose you, and you chose that world. But we can keep our lives separate and together.' And we do and we have." While Parton's career required constant travel, she previously said that Dean preferred staying at their Tennessee home and taking care of their ranch. While speaking with ET, Parton shared that the time spent apart strengthened their relationship. "Our joke about the fact, when people ask me why it's lasted this long, I say, ‘Because I stay gone,’" she told ET. "And there's a lot of truth in that — the fact that we're not in each other's faces all the time. "But we do have a great respect and admiration for each other. We both have a great sense of humor. So, we have a lot of fun," she added. During a 2015 interview with People magazine, Parton shed some light on their favorite shared activities and their low-key home life. DOLLY PARTON CANCELS LAS VEGAS RESIDENCY AS HEALTH ISSUES FORCE HER TO STEP BACK FROM STAGE PERFORMANCES "We like to get out in our little RV and just be simple," she said. "I love to read, I love to cook, I love to be with my husband. I put on my little comfy clothes – I call them my baby clothes – and we just relax." "He loves to go on vacation or on little trips, but he doesn’t want to be gone a long time," Parton continued. "He wants to be mostly around the house. He knows I’m just the opposite. I can’t go enough places. I can’t do enough things. He loves that. He’s independent." "But when we’re together, we have enough things in common that it works," she added. "We love the simple life. We can be calm and just have a good time." Though Dean stayed out of the spotlight, his influence could be heard throughout Parton’s music. The country star previously said that a flirtatious red-haired bank teller’s interest in her husband helped inspire the story behind her 1973 hit "Jolene," while an early disagreement about Parton’s romantic past led her to write 1968's "Just Because I’m a Woman." She later said she thought of Dean while writing her 2012 song "From Here to the Moon and Back." Dean’s love of rock music, particularly Led Zeppelin, also helped inspire Parton’s 2023 album "Rockstar." Shortly after his death, she paid tribute to him with "If You Hadn’t Been There," a song crediting him with supporting her and encouraging her dreams. Parton and Dean never had children, though she said they had imagined becoming parents early in their marriage and even chosen names. In 2017, Parton told The Guardian that they would have named a daughter Carla. The "9 to 5" star previously said that she later came to believe not having kids allowed her to pursue her career and devote herself to other children, including her nieces and nephews and goddaughter Miley Cyrus, as well as those reached through her early-childhood literacy program Imagination Library. "I didn’t have children because I believed that God didn’t mean for me to have kids, so everybody’s kids could be mine, so I could do things like Imagination Library, because if I hadn’t had the freedom to work, I wouldn’t have done all the things I’ve done," she said while appearing on 2020 episode of Apple TV+’s "The Oprah Conversation." "I wouldn’t be in a position to do all of the things I’m doing now." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE In May 2016, Parton and Dean renewed their vows in a private Nashville ceremony on their 50th anniversary. "We’re going to get married again!" Parton told People magazine at the time. "I’ll have a beautiful wedding dress, ’cause I didn’t have a big, long wedding dress when we got married, and we've got a suit for him, so we’re going to dress up and take a bunch of pictures." Parton later celebrated their vow renewal ceremony in a June 2016 statement. "If I had it to do all over, I’d do it all over again, and we did," she said. "I’m dragging him kicking and screaming into the next 50 years." On March 3, 2025, Parton announced Dean's death on social media, writing, "Carl and I spent many wonderful years together." "Words can't do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years," she added. Thank you for your prayers and sympathy." Days later, Parton released "If You Hadn't Been There" in honor of her husband and the cover art for the song featured a vintage photo of the couple. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I fell in love with Carl Dean when I was 18 years old," she wrote on Instagram at the time. "We have spent 60 precious and meaningful years together. Like all great love stories, they never end. They live on in memory and song. He will always be the star of my life story, and I dedicate this song to him." Though no cause of death was disclosed, Parton later said her husband had "suffered a lot" during his final years. During a June 2025 interview with The Associated Press, Parton opened up about how her belief in God has helped her navigate the grief she has endured in the wake of Dean's death. "I am a person of faith, and I truly believe that I’m going to see him again someday," Parton said. In the months after Dean’s death, Parton revealed that she had neglected her own health while caring for her husband during his prolonged illness. She later battled a kidney stone infection and other health complications that forced her to postpone concerts and miss public appearances. However, Parton continued working and remained optimistic about her recovery until shortly before her death. articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan waived Rs.42 lakh bill for 'Deool Band 2'; makers donate profits to farmers’ children
articles.summary: Director Pravin Tarde disclosed that after ‘Deool Band 2’ surpassed the Rs 100 crore mark at the box office, the makers chose to donate the entire pro.
articles.body: Director Pravin Tarde disclosed that after ‘Deool Band 2’ surpassed the Rs 100 crore mark at the box office, the makers chose to donate the entire profit earned once production costs were covered. As per the filmmaker, these proceeds were channeled towards funding the education of children whose farmer parents died by suicide. Tarde, who had earlier shared that the film might never have been released without Shah Rukh Khan stepping in to help, opened up about both the movie's success and this charitable gesture.‘Deool Band 2’ makers donate entire profitIn a conversation with Pinkvilla, Tarde shared, "What made Deool Band 2 a unique film across India? The film earned Rs 100 crore. We only took the production cost for ourselves. However, every single penny that we earned from that film as profit was donated." He went on to explain that the funds were directed towards supporting the education of children whose farmer parents died by suicide. "We donated it to the kids of the farmers who died by suicide. It was donated with the intention that they could resume their education. We started distributing money to kids belonging to drought-hit areas of Maharashtra," he added.‘Deool Band 2’ team provides meals to 250 childrenTarde further shared that the team, using the film's earnings, ensures around 250 children receive two meals a day, and intends to keep this effort running in the years ahead. He gave credit to producer Kailash Vani for backing the initiative.‘Deool Band 2’ faced a budget hurdle before releaseA shortage of funds turned out to be a serious roadblock right before the film's release. The team was unable to bear the cost of Rs 42 lakh charged by Shah Rukh Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment for the Digital Cinema Package (DCP), a mandatory format for screening films on digital projectors. While they had planned for an expense of roughly Rs 12 lakh, the quoted amount turned out to be almost three-and-a-half times higher, at nearly Rs 42 lakh.Pravin Tarde recalls the tough phaseLooking back at the tough phase, Tarde shared with Abhijat Marathi Filmy, “The bill came to Rs 42 lakh. We didn’t have that kind of money, nor did we have any source from where we could arrange it. We approached Red Chillies and explained our situation. We told them that it was a Marathi film, a regional film, and our budget was limited. But we wanted to release it on a large scale and requested their support.”Their appeal eventually made its way to Shah Rukh Khan himself. Tarde recounted that the actor inquired with his technical team about the situation. "They told him it was a film by the makers of Mulshi Pattern. Since Mulshi Pattern was later remade as Antim by Salman Khan, Shah Rukh was aware of our work. He then enquired about Deool Band 2. His team told him it was a well-made emotional film and that the makers wanted the DCP but couldn't afford the cost. The DCP was ready, but it hadn't been handed over because the dues were pending," Tarde said.The filmmaker added: “Shah Rukh Khan simply said, ‘Waive off their bill.’ He told them, ‘It’s a Marathi film. Give them the DCP. We can sort out the payments later. If it’s a good film, give them the DCP.’ They showed tremendous respect towards Marathi cinema. For him, the film was more important than the money. I credit all these people for the success of the film.”Deool Band 2's budget and theme‘Deool Band 2’, a social commentary that addressed the issue of farmer suicides, was reportedly produced on a budget of Rs 8-10 crore.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Quote of the day by Clint Eastwood: ‘As you get older, you're not afraid of doubt. Doubt isn't running the show,' the ‘Piano’ actor’s insightful words on how age brings maturity to deal with uncertainty in a better way
articles.summary: Discover Clint Eastwood's insightful perspective on how aging transforms our relationship with doubt and uncertainty, fostering maturity and resilience in decision-making.
articles.body: When we are younger, doubt and uncertainty may often leave you feeling as if your life is being driven by negative emotions. However, Clint Eastwood challenges this ideology and says that as you grow older, you learn how to deal with these emotions in a better and more mature way. While doubt never truly goes away from your life, it can certainly stop becoming a driving force for your decisions. From serving in the military and doing odd jobs to becoming one of the most iconic Hollywood veterans, Eastwood has lived a long life and summed up the idea of navigating life’s uncertainties with grit and determination with today’s quote.Clint Eastwood’s inspirational quote reads, "As you get older, you're not afraid of doubt. Doubt isn't running the show.”What does Clint Eastwood’s quote mean?Clint Eastwood discusses how age brings an unavoidable sense of maturity and adulthood. He shared these words in a 2008 interview with Esquire.One of the most common emotions that plagues us throughout our lives, no matter what, is doubt. However, Eastwood suggests with this quote that our relationship with uncertainty shifts as we age and gain experience. You cannot change the fact that it will remain a constant part of your life; however, the way you deal with that emotion as you grow older will certainly change and get better with time.In your youth, uncertainty and doubt often drive the things you do; however, as you gain more wisdom, you do not have to let them drive your decisions and actions. As you get older, doubt evolves from a driving force into a passive emotion. Age provides you with a vast portfolio of past experiences, proving that even when things go wrong, you can adapt, survive, and recalibrate. Doubt no longer signals imminent danger; it simply signals that an outcome is unwritten. As you grow older, doubt becomes a prompt to prepare or pay attention, not a reason to quit.At the end of the day, the quote from the beloved veteran actor is about this: Rather than wasting energy trying to eliminate doubt, a more mature and developed mindset accepts doubt as something that cannot be avoided in an unpredictable world. You acknowledge that it exists, step past it, and gain full control over your decisions. Growing older brings on a sense of maturity that you may not have had in your youth.About Clint Eastwood’s early lifeClint Eastwood was born on May 31, 1930, in San Francisco, California, during the Great Depression. His father, Clinton Eastwood Sr, used to work as a manufacturing worker, while his mother, Ruth, used to work in clerical roles. His childhood was filled with a lot of instability as the family moved around a lot for his father’s work. After a while, the family settled down in a high-end neighbourhood in Piedmont, California, during the 1940s.After graduating from high school, the actor worked many odd jobs, including lifeguard, paperboy, grocery clerk, golf caddy, and forest firefighter, before he was drafted during the Korean War.Clint Eastwood’s career and legacyThe actor met Chuck Hill while he was in the army, who in turn helped him connect with people in the entertainment industry. Even though he did not have any prior experience in acting, director Arthur Libin at the time was heavily interested in his movie-star-like appearance. He told him to enrol in acting classes, which he did, and after a while he landed his first role in ‘Revenge of the Creature.’ He later landed another major role in the comedy-drama film ‘Ginger Rogers.’He rose to fame in 1959, when he landed a role in the series 'Rawhide.' Some of his other iconic roles at the time included ‘A Fistful of Dollars,' ‘For A Few More Dollars,' ‘The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly,' ‘Paint Your Wagon,' ‘Two Mules for Sister Sara,' ‘Play Misty for Me,' ‘Dirty Harry,' 'Unforgiven,' ‘Million Dollar Baby,' ‘Every Which Way But Loose,' ‘The Outlaw Josey Wales,' ‘The Bridges of Madison County,' ‘Gran Torino,' ‘In the Line of Fire,' ‘Dollars Trilogy,' ‘Man With No Name,' ‘Hang 'Em High,' and many others.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Gigi Hadid says her relationship with Bradley Cooper provides something she hasn't experienced before
articles.summary: Gigi Hadid told Vogue France that deep honesty sets her Bradley Cooper romance apart, as marriage speculation swirls after their Paris ring sighting.
articles.body: Gigi Hadid is getting candid about what makes her romance with Bradley Cooper unlike the relationships that came before him. In a new interview with Vogue France, the 31-year-old supermodel offered a rare glimpse inside her notoriously private relationship with the Oscar-nominated actor. "What is beautiful about my current relationship, and so different from what I have experienced, is an ability to be deeply honest," Hadid told the outlet. "To say what you think, when you think it." GOLDIE HAWN CREDITS ‘FREEDOM’ FOR KEEPING 43-YEAR RELATIONSHIP WITH KURT RUSSELL STRONG When the interviewer noted that kind of honesty isn't always easy, Hadid didn't hesitate. "I know. But if that's impossible, it probably means he's not the right person," she said. Hadid's candid comments come weeks after she and Cooper, 51, fueled marriage speculation when they were photographed in Paris wearing matching bands on their left ring fingers. Page Six reported earlier this month that the rings were Boucheron wedding bands, though neither Hadid nor Cooper publicly confirmed that they had tied the knot. Days later, Us Weekly reported, according to a source, that the jewelry was instead a pair of "promise rings" and that the couple was not married. The pair, who have been romantically linked since late 2023, have largely kept their relationship away from the spotlight. Hadid told Vogue in 2025 that the couple's decision to remain private wasn't necessarily strategic. "It's just not part of our relationship to share for whatever reason," she said at the time, describing their relationship as "very romantic and happy." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE That privacy began to shift in May 2025, when Hadid made the romance Instagram official while celebrating her 30th birthday. The model shared a series of photos from her birthday party, including one of her and Cooper kissing in front of a multi-tiered cake. "I feel so lucky to be 30!" Hadid wrote at the time. "I feel so lucky for every high and low, for all the lessons and gifts both have brought me." She added that she felt "so lucky to be a mom, friend, partner, sister, daughter, colleague to some of the most unbelievable humans." Now, more than a year later, Hadid appears to be settling into a quieter chapter. Asked by Vogue France how she was feeling, Hadid said friends have noticed a change. "Right now my friends are saying to me: ‘Gigi, what's going on? Looks like you're 19 again,’" she said. "I just think I'm... serene." OLIVIA WILDE BREAKS SILENCE ON HARRY STYLES FANS AND THEIR BRUTAL REACTION TO THEIR 10-YEAR AGE GAP ROMANCE Part of that serenity appears to come from the life she has built away from the fashion industry's constant spotlight. Hadid told the outlet that spending time in the countryside with her daughter, partner, friends and animals helps ground her before she returns to work. "Living in the countryside surrounded by animals, with my daughter, my partner, my friends, is part of what recharges my batteries," she said. "It allows me to appreciate the richness of fashion when I come back to it." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Hadid shares daughter Khai with ex-boyfriend Zayn Malik, while Cooper shares daughter Lea with former partner Irina Shayk. The model also said she and Cooper talk about their careers even if they don't always fully understand the demands of the other's profession. "We don't necessarily understand all the challenges of each other's job, but the main thing is to have someone who supports you – and helps you keep your feet on the ground," Hadid told Vogue France. When asked whether a strong relationship requires work from both people, Hadid offered another perspective. "I would say it's a trip for two," she said. Her latest comments echo what she previously said about finding a partner who already understands what he wants from life. "Knowing what you want and deserve in a relationship is essential, and then to find someone that is in a place in their life where they know what they want and deserve…and you both do work separately to come together and be the best partner that you can be," Hadid previously told Vogue. "I just feel really lucky. Yeah, lucky's the word." The couple's romance has also given Hadid a new way of experiencing one of the cities most closely associated with her career. For years, she said Paris primarily meant work. "I landed there, drove to the hotel where twenty photographers were waiting for me, impossible to walk, then in a car to a windowless studio," Hadid told Vogue France. That changed through Cooper, whom she described as someone who loves France and speaks French. HEIDI KLUM SHUNS HOLLYWOOD'S WEIGHT-LOSS OBSESSION AFTER HUSBAND TOM KAULITZ TOLD HER TO 'EAT MORE' PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "Except that, recently, thanks to my boyfriend who loves France and speaks French, I discovered a completely different Paris that I adore," she said. Asked whether she could envision living there, Hadid didn't rule it out. "So at some point, why not move there, yes..." she said. Hadid's growing sense of peace also extends to how she views fame and the image of her life presented to millions of followers online. "99% of my daily life is not online," she told Vogue France. "What I'm posting is my way of celebrating the wonderful things in life. But Instagram remains 1% of my life." The model has lived much of her adult life in the public eye, becoming one of the industry's most recognizable faces while still in her teens. She told Vogue France that the visibility she once dreamed about eventually became overwhelming. "It was around the age of 19 that this visibility began," Hadid said. "At first, it's true that this is what you dream of. And, little by little, the noose tightens. You lose control." "And it becomes overwhelming, because you end up only living through the eyes of others," she continued. These days, Hadid said she has found a better balance between fame and her private life. "Today, I have found a balance between my life as a mom in Pennsylvania and my public life," she said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Navy veteran trades military uniform for Miss Georgia sash following heartbreaking loss
articles.summary: Jade Kircus, a former naval officer and mother of three, is competing in the Miss USA pageant after experiencing a miscarriage.
articles.body: After eight years of serving her country in a Navy uniform, Jade Kircus is trading it for a pageant sash. At 36, the wife and mother of three is representing Georgia in her first-ever pageant: Miss USA. The competition takes place Aug. 27 in Miami. "To be quite honest, I've actually never considered doing pageants," the Navy veteran told Fox News Digital. "It's not that I didn't think they were wonderful, and I really admired the women who did them. I just was always in a season where I wasn't able to do them, and I'm finally in a season where I can give a hundred percent." MISS AMERICA DEFENDS PAGEANT MAKEUP AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA TROLLS TOOK AIM "I went from the Navy uniform to being in a sash because I really felt like the Lord put it in my heart in October to compete," she said. "And when I found out that my state didn't have an actual pageant, I signed up for the open casting call after praying about it for a long time. So, since October, I've prayed about it. And the door opened. I joined the open casting call and was selected as Miss Georgia USA." Kircus said it's never too late to chase a dream — or a crown. "I never thought that at this point in my life I would be doing something like this," she said. "But you can do hard things. You can do hard things at any age, at any stage. And I think each person has their own season where they're able to step out, and they're able to really show up in a way that they never thought they could. And so, whoever is listening, I want you to know that today you can make a choice to change. Today, you can make a choice to be confident and become the woman or the man that God has called you to be. It's never too late." WATCH: MISS GEORGIA USA SHARES JOURNEY FROM NAVY UNIFORM TO PAGEANT SASH In October, Kircus decided to take a chance on pageants. Later that month, she learned she was pregnant. "I said, 'OK, Lord, that's a closed door,'" she recalled. Months later, Kircus experienced a heartbreaking loss. In January, she had a miscarriage nearly 16 weeks into her pregnancy. "We lost our baby girl," she said, fighting back tears. "I remember holding her in the hospital through several traumatic moments before that. And I remember looking at her and being like, 'Wow, this life is so beautiful.' And it was in my most difficult moment that the Lord really showed up and showed me who He was. And although it was challenging, I clung to my faith." Kircus said her faith helped her through the loss, giving her "peace" and strength to keep moving forward for her family. "In my hardest moment, I looked at that and was like, 'God, you're still faithful. You're still good. You still care about me deeply, and my baby girl is with you. I get to meet her one day because you're good.'" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Kircus said she spent January grieving. By February, she was ready to take a leap of faith and give herself something new to work toward. "In February, God put Miss USA back in my heart," she said. "I'm like, 'OK, God, I thought it was a closed door, but it is an open door. And so, I'm not going to sit in the pain and the hard parts of what I just experienced. I'm going to move forward and know that you have a plan.'" "I miss my baby girl, and I wish I was holding her right now," she said. "I know that I'm here for a purpose, whatever that is, whatever that looks like." Pageantry is far different from Navy service, but Kircus said her training prepared her for the challenge. "The Navy really taught me determination," she said. "It taught me resilience. It taught me how to lead with purpose, no matter the circumstances. Being a mother has also taught me those things, but it taught me so much about people, taught me how to love people even better, taught me how to raise the next generation, how to meet them where they're at, let them know they're valued, they have worth, they're loved." "The Miss USA organization has taught me so much," she said. "Not only about just being able to step out and be bold wherever you're at, but also how to relate to people, how to truly be the best version of myself and not only lead people, but work with them to make a better community, a better world." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Kircus is a first-generation American whose parents are from Scotland and England. She served two sea tours before completing a shore tour at U.S. Central Command in Tampa. After leaving the Navy in 2020 and working for several years as a government contractor, Kircus chose to become a stay-at-home mother in 2024. The Miss USA pageant dates to 1952, when Catalina Swimwear launched the competition after withdrawing its sponsorship of Miss America. For Kircus, competing for the crown is another opportunity to serve. "Not only have I experienced that as a naval officer, but I've experienced it as a daughter, as somebody who has parents who are not originally from this country. My heart has always been to serve, and representing the USA on an international scale really would be such an honor. And I do believe we can make an impact." articles.title: Kylie Jenner Reveals She Wants Bigger Boobs—Here Are the Details on Her Current Breast Augmentation
articles.summary: What exactly "445 cc, moderate profile, half under the muscle" means.
articles.body:
Kylie Jenner used to be secretive about her plastic surgery procedures and tweakments—who can forget when she denied lip filler rumors up until 2015 ? But now that Jenner is older and society's views on cosmetic surgery have changed, the Khy founder has turned into an open book .

On a new episode of Better Half with Stas & Vic , Stas Karanikolaou and Victoria Villarroel's podcast, Jenner revealed she wants bigger breast implants. "I do want them bigger," she said. "I say it every day. I'm like, 'They need to be bigger and more out there.' I want my tits to walk in before I do." Karanikolaou joked that Jenner "has an obsession with big tits." Jenner, 29, said that she's "probably not" going to get her breasts done again before she turns 30.

But in the meantime, we know the exact specifications of her current implants, thanks to a TikTok interaction last summer, when a fan asked Jenner about the details behind her breast augmentation . "Girl, please can you just tell us what it is that you asked for when you had your boobs done," the TikToker Rachel Leary said in a video. She called it the most "perfect, natural-looking boob job ever."

Jenner herself commented on the TikTok with the details: "445 cc, moderate profile, half under the muscle!!! Silicone!!! Garth Fisher!!! Hope this helps lol." If you're wondering what exactly that means—for your own knowledge or because you're hoping to take Jenner's words to your plastic surgeon—we spoke with a few experts to break it all down:

"445 cc is the size, measured by volume," says John Diaz , MD, a Beverly Hills-based board-certified plastic surgeon. "A 'cc' means cubic centimeters." A large implant is often considered to be anything over 400 cc, so 445 cc is a fairly substantial augmentation. While it can't be directly translated to a new cup size (as it depends what you're starting with), you can expect a 445 cc implant to add close to two cup sizes to your initial breast volume.

When you're getting a breast augmentation, the "profile" is how much the implant juts out from your chest while you're standing. "When it comes to profiles, there are different types, such as low, moderate, and high, which are decided upon based on the patient's anatomy and the goal they're trying to achieve," explains Lyle Leipziger, MD, chief of plastic surgery at North Shore University Hospital and LIJ Medical Center. A moderate profile breast implant is typically considered one of the most natural profiles to get, and will have slightly more projection than a low-profile implant but look more natural than some of the higher-profile options.

"Many breast augmentations today are dual plane, meaning part under the muscle and part under the lower breast tissue," Leipziger adds. In a dual plane breast augmentation, the upper part of the breast implant is inserted below the pectoral muscle, while the lower part is just under the breast tissue. "Half under the muscle" is considered one of the most natural-looking placement methods.

When Jenner says "silicone," she's talking about the material of the implant she used. There are many different options, including saline implants (which are filled with salt water), gummy bear implants (which are thicker than traditional silicone implants), and silicone implants (which Jenner has). Silicone implants are filled with silicone gel and are meant to feel the most like natural breast tissue. "This implant is likely an Allergan implant, which is the most common implant used at our facility," says Oren Tepper, MD, board-certified plastic surgeon and founder of Greenwich Street 497 . "One of the advantages of Allergan implants are the three cohesive [silicone] gel options, which provide a natural feel and look, and the wide range of options provided, which can be tailored to each patient's specific anatomy." Word to the wise: If you want silicone implants too, you may need to have more check-ups with your doctor to get an MRI to make sure the silicone isn't leaking into your body.

In a world where plastic surgery is becoming increasingly common, Jenner's transparency is refreshing—and makes talking to your own plastic surgeon about what you want just a little bit easier.
